name: Virtual Private Network (VPN)
description: The adversary is leveraging Virtual Private Networks (VPN) to hide the origin of the activities.

subtechniques.name: Avoid free VPN services
subtechniques.description: Free VPN providers might collect and sell your information.

subtechniques.name: dVPN
subtechniques.description: Decentralized VPN: dVPNs use blockchain technology to operate a network of distributed nodes to connect to, and aim to improve on VPN service design in other ways. Current solutions promise proven inability for centralized logging, distribution of trust without one entity making decisions, and more fair payment systems. They aim for these improvements and highlight them as selling points while promising to deliver the same benefits as a centralized VPN service.

subtechniques.name: Free VPN service
subtechniques.description: Free VPN services might be used to mask IP-addresses or to add them to proxy/vpn chains.

subtechniques.name: IPtables kill switch
subtechniques.description: A VPN kill switch might be implemented with IP tables on Linux systems. This prevents IP address leakages.

subtechniques.name: Killswitch VPN
subtechniques.description: A kill switch is a feature that blocks your internet access if the VPN connection drops, preventing your data from being exposed

subtechniques.name: Nested chain of VPNs
subtechniques.description: choose providers that operate from poorly-cooperating geopolitical spheres of influence (SOIs). It’s best to avoid providers in the SOI where you live. For your direct-connect VPN, it’s arguably best to choose a provider in a relatively-neutral SOI, which doesn’t attract too much attention, and yet is at least somewhat hard to subvert. For your terminal/innermost VPN, it’s arguably best to choose a provider in an effectively non-cooperating SOI. If you’re using three or more VPNs overall, it’s arguably best to alternate between distinct poorly-cooperating SOIs for the middle VPNs.

subtechniques.name: No-log VPN
subtechniques.description: VPN-services which do not keep logs are preferred to prevent leaving any traces.

subtechniques.name: Non-USA VPN
subtechniques.description: USA VPN-providers are forced to provide law enforcement agencies logs, therefore they must be avoided.

subtechniques.name: Route VM's through host VPN
subtechniques.description: Virtual machines might be routed through the host VPN connection.

subtechniques.name: Second VPN service
subtechniques.description: Secondary VPN services might be added to virtual machines to avoid leaks during the host-client to VM-client transition.

subtechniques.name: Stealth mode VPN
subtechniques.description: Stealth mode VPN’s try to use undetectable VPN protocols.

subtechniques.name: VPN -> obfs4 bridge
subtechniques.description: For optimized fingerprint protection, a obfs4 bridge might be user after a VPN tunnel.

subtechniques.name: VPN qube
subtechniques.description: VPN’s might be setup in specific qubes in Qubes OS to provide internet connectivity to other qubes.

subtechniques.name: VPN routers
subtechniques.description: A VPN router is simply a router that has been configured to automatically connect to VPN servers, thus protecting your whole network.

subtechniques.name: VPN-firewall
subtechniques.description: VPN-firewall: If you’re going with the high-privacy option, just disable Internet connectivity to your LAN. After finishing the installation, you’ll install VPN-Firewall and your direct-connect VPN client, restore Internet connectivity, and establish the VPN connection. Then you’ll download and install updates, reboot and proceed to the next tutorial for VirtualBox setup.
